# WSI Profile 1: surfaces, presentation and what comes back

Specification hash: `e1c658c607f3837e413cf32165904ec5447c929172b05160bf8c70a23732d60d`

This is the contract between an application that draws and the service that puts what it drew on a
screen. Every number in it is one two sides round differently if it is not stated, and every state is
one an implementation discovers it needed after shipping.

## Logical, physical and the scale between them

A surface has THREE sizes and not one. A phone surface is 400 x 800 logical at scale 3.0 and
1200 x 2400 physical; an application that cannot see those as three numbers either renders at the
wrong size or renders blurred.

| question | answer |
| --- | --- |
| how the scale is represented | `{ numerator: u32, denominator: u32 }, exact, never a float on the wire` |
| which extent is authoritative | physical; the logical extent is derived from it and the scale, and never the other way round |
| where an edge lands | an edge at logical coordinate `l` is the physical coordinate `round_half_away_from_zero(l * numerator / denominator)`, computed in integers from the ratio and never from a rounded float, so both neighbours of a shared edge compute the same number |
| how damage rounds | left and top round down, right and bottom round up; conservative, and not a promise of non-overlap between independently rounded geometry |
| how input maps back | a physical input coordinate maps to logical by the exact inverse ratio, rounding half away from zero, after the output transform is undone |

The output transforms are `Normal`, `Rotate90`, `Rotate180`, `Rotate270`, `FlippedNormal`, `FlippedRotate90`, `FlippedRotate180`, `FlippedRotate270`.

## The configuration snapshot

Configuration arrives as ONE snapshot, atomically. A client never applies a new scale with an old
extent, which is what atomic is for.

| field | invalidates images | why it is in the snapshot |
| --- | :---: | --- |
| serial | no | what an acknowledgement names; a stale or unknown serial is refused rather than applied |
| generation | no | which image generation this configuration belongs to; every present carries one and it must match |
| logical extent | yes | what an application lays out in |
| physical extent | yes | what the backend rasterises; the authoritative one |
| scale | yes | the ratio between them, exact |
| transform | yes | the output's orientation, which input mapping is the inverse of |
| output | no | which output the surface is on, so a client can follow its refresh interval |
| presentable pixel format | yes | immutable within a generation; changing it is a new generation |
| colour information | no | the space AND the luminances, because a colour-space name alone cannot tone map |
| subpixel layout | no | which geometry an LCD mask may be rasterised for, and `None` when it is unknown |
| visibility | no | whether this surface is the visible one; acquiring from a hidden surface answers NotVisible |
| focus | no | focus is a property of a SURFACE and not of a connection |

The lifecycle is: configure(snapshot) -> rebuild -> ack_configure(serial) -> first present Full; a present names its configuration serial and its image generation, and both must match the acknowledged current configuration at acceptance.

The colour information is `colour space`, `SDR white luminance in cd/m²`, `minimum luminance in cd/m²`, `maximum luminance in cd/m²`, `maximum frame-average luminance in cd/m²` - because a colour-space NAME is not enough to tone map with: a
conversion that does not know the destination's luminance is guessing at the one number that decides
how the image looks.

## Events

| event | carries | why it is its own event |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Configure` | one SurfaceConfiguration snapshot | the atomic set above; the client rebuilds and acknowledges by serial |
| `ImageAvailable` | nothing | what a client waits on INSTEAD of blocking inside acquire, which is what keeps one dispatch loop alive |
| `PresentComplete` | the present's serial, its outcome and its timestamp evidence | a present's fate is reported per present rather than inferred from the next acquire |
| `CloseRequested` | nothing | a REQUEST and not a teardown: the application decides, which is what makes an unsaved-changes prompt possible |
| `VisibilityChanged` | the new visibility | a background client stops drawing rather than discovering it by a refusal |
| `FocusChanged` | whether this surface has focus | focus belongs to the surface, so the event does too |

at most ONE surface is visible and scanout-bound; other surfaces keep independent resources, generations and queues while hidden, acquiring from them answers NotVisible, frames accepted before a visibility change still settle in FIFO order with the appropriate discarded outcome, and focus belongs to the visible surface.

## The present queue

| state | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Available` | the queue owns it and it can be acquired |
| `Acquired` | the client owns it and may draw into it |
| `PendingPresent` | the service owns it; it has been accepted and not yet completed |
| `Stale` | it belongs to a generation that no longer exists and is never presented into a new one |

| from | on | to | why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Available` | acquire | `Acquired` | the ordinary path |
| `Acquired` | present | `PendingPresent` | the ordinary path; `present` CONSUMES the acquired image, so there is no safe path back to the pixels |
| `PendingPresent` | released | `Available` | the service is done with it, whatever the outcome was |
| `Acquired` | abandon | `Available` | a client that acquired and then decided not to draw returns it without presenting a frame nobody wanted |
| `Available` | generation changed | `Stale` | its extent, scale, orientation or format is not the current one |
| `Acquired` | generation changed | `Stale` | the client discards it rather than presenting it into a generation it was not drawn for |
| `PendingPresent` | generation changed | `Stale` | it completes or is discarded FIRST - a frame in flight is not un-submitted - and is then stale |
| `Stale` | reclaimed | `Available` | the queue rebuilds its images for the new generation |

The Rust shape is what makes the machine unrepresentable when wrong rather than merely documented:
`acquire_next` returns an OWNED acquired image, drawing borrows it, and `present` CONSUMES it - so
after presenting there is no safe path to the pixels until the queue hands them back.

`acquire_next` answers: an image; Again, when none is available - the client waits on ImageAvailable rather than inside the call; NotVisible, when the surface is occluded or in the background; OutOfDate, when the configuration has moved on.

Images are NEGOTIATED - the service advertises a minimum and a maximum, the client requests, the
service answers with the actual - and v1 advertises `min_images = 2` and `max_images = 3`. A
service free to answer one would turn the double-or-triple-buffering gate into a test of nothing.
The present modes are `Fifo`; `Mailbox` and `Immediate` have a PLACE rather than a meaning, so adding one later is not an
argument about what the enumeration was for.

## What a present is worth

FIFO is the order of ACCEPTED presents, by present-call order and not by acquire order; while visible every accepted frame reaches logical presentation, and while occluded or backgrounded new acquires answer NotVisible and already-accepted frames still complete IN ORDER, possibly as discarded.

| outcome | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Displayed` | it reached logical presentation; on a backend that cannot observe scanout this means DRIVER-COMPLETED |
| `DiscardedOccluded` | it was accepted while visible and completed while not; it kept its place in the order and never reached a screen |
| `ReplacedByResize` | a generation change overtook it |
| `DriverLost` | the backend went away under it |

"Displayed" runs three different facts together, and a backend that cannot observe the third says so:

| fact | observable on the current backend | meaning |
| --- | :---: | --- |
| Accepted | yes | the service took the frame and it has a place in the order |
| DriverCompleted | yes | the backend acknowledged the commands that carried it |
| PhysicallyDisplayed | no | a scanout of this frame was observed |

A timestamp is reported as `Unavailable`, `Estimated(t)`, `Measured(t)`. every timing field is optional and typed as such; a backend that cannot supply one says so rather than inventing it.

The frame loop is given `preferred frame deadline`, `the output's refresh interval`, `the completed present's timestamp evidence`, `the present outcome` rather than a clock to sleep on.

## Damage

A bounded LIST of at most 16 rectangles with an explicit whole-surface fallback - not one rectangle,
because a client updating two corners of a screen would otherwise send their bounding box, which is
most of the screen. "A small cap" is not an ABI, so the cap is a number and every question a caller
asks at it has an answer:

| question | answer |
| --- | --- |
| what an EMPTY list means | nothing changed: the frame is pixel-identical to the previously presented one, the present is still ordered and still completes, and the service may release the image without copying |
| how the whole surface is spelled | an explicit Full variant, never one rectangle covering the extent - a rectangle can be wrong by a pixel and a variant cannot |
| a rectangle outside the extent | a TYPED invalid, never a silent clamp |
| exceeding the cap | the caller's problem, solved by merging or by sending Full - never the service's, solved by dropping rectangles |
| overlapping rectangles | legal, and may be normalised by the backend |
| what the coordinates are in | the image space of the generation the present belongs to |
| damage relative to WHAT, when consecutive frames are drawn into different images | EVERY PRESENTED IMAGE CONTAINS A COMPLETE VALID FRAME; damage is a HINT about which pixels changed against the previously presented frame and is never permission to leave the rest undefined |
| the first present of a generation | Full |
| whether a backend may merge | it may, when merging is cheaper than transferring separately - what is forbidden is the unconditional union of everything, which turns two corners into most of the screen |

## Completion

Two ordinary channel pairs per SURFACE, created once when the surface is admitted. No new kernel
object, no generic timeline, no ABI number and no signal right.

| pair | client | service |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PRODUCER_READY` | SEND | RECEIVE | WAIT |
| `PRESENT_DONE` | RECEIVE | WAIT | SEND |

each endpoint is created with depth max_images, so at three images at most six messages are queued across both directions. client endpoints carry neither DUPLICATE nor TRANSFER; a safe completion token may move inside its own process, and the raw endpoint is never exposed beside it.

a v1 presentable image is COHERENT CPU-VISIBLE memory: a send is a release and a receive is an acquire, in both directions, and there is no explicit flush or invalidate in the contract because there is no non-coherent import in v1.

## What v1 does not contract

`popup position`, `z-order`, `simultaneous composition`, `a measured presentation timestamp`, `buffer age`, `deferred replies with a pending-call table` - each of them arrives with the compositor or with a capability the current backend does not
have. Naming them is what stops an implementation inventing one and a client depending on it.
